speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your vertigo, can you tell me if the spinning sensation is triggered by specific head movements, and have you experienced any recent hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in the ear on the affected side? Also, were you able to walk steadily during the episode, or did you feel off-balance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
REQUEST TEST: Audiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike maneuver: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back. Audiogram: Within normal limits for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side with normal hearing strongly suggests Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) affecting the left posterior semicircular canal.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
